BEFORE THE GEORGIA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

GEORGIA POWER COMPANY
DOCKET NO. 55378

Distributed Energy Resource Customer-Owned Agreement

BASIS FOR THE ASSERTION THAT THE
INFORMATION SUBMITTED IS A TRADE SECRET

As part of Georgia Power Company’s 2023 Integrated Resource Plan Update in Docket
No. 55378, Georgia Power Company (‘Georgia Power” or the “Company”) is providing the
Distributed Energy Resource (“DER”) Customer-Owned Agreement between Georgia Power and
Atlanta Falcons Football Club, LLC (“DCO Agreement”). The DCO Agreement contains sensitive
contract terms and conditions, customer account information, customer equipment value, pricing
information, and sensitive internal email information (the “Information”). All such Information
constitutes trade secret information of the Southern Company, Georgia Power, its affiliates, and
its counterparty and is therefore protected from public disclosure under Commission Rule 5 15-3-
I-11.

The Information derives economic value from not being generally known to and not being
readily ascertainable by proper means by other persons who can obtain economic value from its
disclosure or use. Specifically, the trade secret portions of the Information contain confidential
contract terms, customer account information, customer equipment value, and pricing information.
This Information is considered confidential by the Company and is not generally known to the
public. Disclosure of the Information would seriously harm the Company’s ability to negotiate
favorable and constructive terms with future customers. If the Information was revealed to the
public, other customers and competitors could use the Information in contract negotiations to
obtain favorable terms to the detriment of customers and the Company. This would ultimately
result in rates and terms that are less economic for all customers. These parties are not required to
disclose similar information and to require Georgia Power to do so would put it at an economic
disadvantage.

Additionally, the Information contains a sensitive, undisclosed email account which is
maintained for infrastructure protection purposes. This Information is considered confidential by
the Company and is not generally known to the public. Disclosure of the Information would
seriously harm the Company by exposing the account to malicious use and unwanted spam.

The trade secret portions of the Information are subject to extensive efforts to maintain
their secrecy. Only select Georgia Power and Southern Company personnel and their legal counsel

 are granted access to this information. Those personnel receive access only on a “need to know”
basis. If a party outside Georgia Power and Southern Company and their legal counsel are granted
access to the trade secret portions of the Information, the party is required to sign a confidentiality
agreement.

Erica L. Stephens, first being duly sworn, deposes and states that she has reviewed the DCO
Agreement included in this filing in Docket No. 55378, and that the specific information
designated as trade secret constitutes trade secrets in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 10-1-761 (2019).

SCHEDULE OF DEFINED TERMS

This DCO Agreement uses the defined terms identified in this Schedule of Defined Terms, or in the body of this DCO Agreement, and the rules of construction described in Section 13.13 (Contract Interpretation).
Access: As defined in Section 5.1 (Access).
Additional or Unforeseen Costs: As defined in Section 8.2 (Additional or Unforeseen Costs). 
Affected Party: The Party impacted by a Force Majeure Event.
Affiliate: For a specific entity, any other entity directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the specified entity; “control” means the power to direct the management and policies of the entity, directly or indirectly, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise. For purposes of this DCO Agreement, it is assumed that the direct or indirect owner of 50% or more of the outstanding stock or other equity interest of an entity has “control” of that entity.
Applicable Standards: Both: (i) all applicable current standards of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), Underwriters Laboratories (UL), NEC, NESC, National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA), American National Standards Institute (ANSI), Federal Communications Commission (FCC), NFPA, other national codes, and any local code pertaining to electrical facility design, construction, or safety; and (ii) the terms and conditions of this DCO Agreement.
Application: As defined in Section 2.1 (Application).
Application Approval Date: The date on which Full and Final Approval is obtained.
BlueBook: The GPC BlueBook for Electrical Service or any successor publicly available on the GPC Distributed Generation Interconnection website.
Business Day: Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays.
Calendar Day: Any calendar day.
Closeout Fee: As defined in Section 9.6 (Closeout Fee; GPC’s Rights Upon Termination or Expiration).
Compliance Incentive: Defined in Section 9.4 (Compliance Incentive).
Commercial Operation: The Customer Equipment is capable of providing Resiliency Service or Grid Support. 
Commercial Operation Date: As defined in Section 4.1 (Customer Equipment; Commercial Operation Date).
Commission: The Georgia Public Service Commission.
Customer: The owner of the Customer Equipment that is the subject of this DCO Agreement and the counterparty to GPC in the Interconnection Agreement. “Customer” in this DCO Agreement is equivalent to “DER Owner” in the Southern Company Policy.
Customer Equipment: As defined in Section 4.1 (Customer Equipment; Commercial Operation Date).
DCO Agreement: This DER Customer-Owned Agreement between the Parties.
DCO Credit: As defined in Section 8.1 (DCO Credit).
Default: Customer’s breach of a DCO Agreement warranty, representation, or covenant or failure to perform a material DCO Agreement obligation that is not timely cured in accordance with Section 9.3 (GPC Termination for Cause).
DER Customer Owned Schedule: The GPC Electric Service Tariff: DER Customer Owned Schedule: “DCO-1” or its successor.
EFC Agreement: If applicable, the excess facilities charge agreement in the form attached as Exhibit C.
Electric System: Any facilities owned or operated by GPC (including any Customer-owned substation or other facilities) or other electric utilities in Georgia or a surrounding state.
Execution Date: The date on which GPC signs this DCO Agreement, as shown on the signature page.
Force Majeure Event: An occurrence, non-occurrence, circumstance, or set of circumstances that is beyond the reasonable control of a Party or its contractor, not reasonably foreseeable, and not caused by the Party’s negligence, inaction, lack of due diligence, breach of this DCO Agreement, or failure to follow Prudent Industry Practices. A Force Majeure Event does not include: (i) inability to meet a legal requirement or the change in a legal requirement; (ii) inability to obtain or maintain, or delay in obtaining, any permit, approval, or other consent required from a governmental authority; (iii) equipment failure or equipment damage in the case of the Customer Equipment or any failure of a Customer or Customer Equipment contractor, supplier, or vendor, unless the failure or damage results directly from an event that would otherwise constitute a Force Majeure Event; (iv) change in market conditions that affects cost or availability of equipment, materials, supplies, or services, unless such cost or availability change results directly from an event that would otherwise constitute a Force Majeure Event; (v) a site-specific strike, walkout, lockout, or other labor dispute at the Customer Equipment; or (vi) failure or inability to obtain or retain sufficient funds for any reason, or Customer’s loss of or inability to obtain or retain any tax credit or other incentive with respect to any portion of the Customer Equipment. Except for an obligation to make payments due, Customer will not be in Default under this DCO Agreement if there is, nor liable for a failure to perform that results from, a Force Majeure Event, if the Party impacted (who bears the burden of proof): (a) promptly provided written notice of the event in accordance with Section 13.7 (Notices and Contacts) and probable consequences; (b) exercised reasonable effort to minimize disruption; and (c) timely resumed performance. Neither Party is liable to the other for loss, damage, or delay resulting from a Force Majeure Event.
Full and Final Approval: Commission approval in the form of a final, non-appealable order, approving this DCO Agreement and certifying all Customer Equipment identified in the SOW as a resource under the DER Customer Owned Schedule, without qualifications or conditions and acceptable to GPC in GPC’s sole discretion.
Governmental Entity: A governmental entity of the state of Georgia or political subdivision thereof.
GPC: Georgia Power Company, a Georgia corporation, which is a subsidiary of Southern Company, or any permitted successor or assign. “Company” is the equivalent term in the Southern Company Policy.
GPC Equipment: Ancillary devices or equipment installed by GPC at or around the Site to enable GPC to provide the Services.
GPC-Related Party: Each of GPC, Southern Company, and their Affiliates, and the officers, directors, employees, representatives, and agents of each of them. 
Grid Support: Dispatch of the Customer Equipment during any period in which an Outage Event is not occurring to allow GPC to provide system benefits to all GPC customers.  
Interconnection Agreement: The Distributed Energy Resource (DER) Customer-Owned (DCO) Program Interconnection Agreement between the Parties related to the Customer Equipment that is the subject of this DCO Agreement.
Late Payment Charge: As defined in Section 8.3 (Late Payment).
Losses: Any and all liability, proceedings, suits, cost, or expense for loss, damage, or injury to persons or property.

Minimum Technical Requirements: The Minimum Specifications, together with applicable portions of the current version of the: (i) Southern Company Policy; (ii) BlueBook; and (iii) the Test Policy. These GPC Technical Requirements are complementary, but if there is a discrepancy, the order of precedence is, as applicable: (a) the Rules and Regulations; (b) Southern Company Policy; (c) BlueBook; and (d) Test Policy. SOW: The Statement of Work attached as Exhibit A (Statement of Work).
Studies: As defined in the Recitals.
Term: The time period during which this DCO Agreement is effective, commencing on the Execution Date and continuing until the date specified in Exhibit A (Statement of Work).
Test Policy: The GPC Distribution Test Policy or any successor policy, publicly available on the GPC Distributed Generation Interconnection website.
Witness Testing: Live testing of the Customer Equipment while operating in parallel with the Electric System, in accordance with the Test Policy. 

Distributed Energy Resource (DER) 
Customer-Owned (DCO) Program Agreement
at DCO-00001 (Atlanta Falcons Training Camp)
between Georgia Power Company
and Atlanta Falcons Football Club, LLC
Georgia Power Company, a Georgia corporation and Atlanta Falcons Football Club, LLC, a Georgia limited liability company enter into this DER Customer-Owned Agreement (“DCO Agreement”) effective as of the Execution Date. GPC and Customer acknowledge:
Customer desires to: (i) participate in the DER Customer Owned Schedule; (ii) install the Customer Equipment meeting the Minimum Technical Requirements and interconnect with the Electric System’s distribution facilities, as the equipment and requirements are further described in the SOW; (iii) allow GPC to dispatch the Customer Equipment to exclusively provide Resiliency Service to Customer if Customer experiences an Outage Event at Customer’s facility or facilities located at the location(s) identified in the SOW (each, a “Site”); and (iv) enable GPC to exclusively dispatch the Customer Equipment during any period in which an Outage Event is not occurring to allow GPC to provide Grid Support.
Customer has caused to be conducted one or more studies to evaluate the Customer Equipment’s impact (including operational, interconnection-related, and other cost impacts) on the Electrical System and the Customer Equipment’s capabilities to provide the Services (collectively, the “Studies”).
In consideration of the mutual promises described here, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt, adequacy, and sufficiency of which each Party acknowledges, and intending to be legally bound, the Parties agree: 
TERM
Term
. This DCO Agreement will become effective on the Execution Date and will, unless terminated in accordance with Part 9 (DCO Agreement Suspension, Expiration, or Termination), continue after the Commercial Operation Date for the Term.
Term Extensions
. At least 180 Calendar Days before the end of the Term, either Party may provide the other Party with written notice of its desire to extend the Term of this DCO Agreement, subject to modifications (including term and price) to be agreed upon by GPC and Customer, and subject to then-existing Commission rules and regulations and the Rules and Regulations. If a Party provides the other Party with timely notice of its desire to extend the Term and the other Party likewise desires to extend the Term (in its sole discretion), the Parties will negotiate in good faith to reach an agreement on the terms of any mutually desired extension. If the Parties have failed to reach an agreement as to the terms of the extension by the expiration of the then-current Term, this DCO Agreement will automatically extend on a month-to-month basis until the first to occur of: (i) the date on which the Parties execute a written amendment to extend the Term; or (ii) the date either Party provides written notice to the other Party that the notifying Party no longer desires to extend the Term.
COMMISSION APPLICATION; CONDITIONS
Application
. At a time mutually agreed upon by the Parties, GPC will submit an application (the “Application”) to the Commission for Full and Final Approval. GPC, in its sole discretion, will determine the manner in which it submits the Application and Customer will use commercially reasonable efforts to support the Application. If Full and Final Approval has not been obtained within 180 Calendar Days after the date on which the Commission deems the Application to have been filed, consistent with the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-5, then GPC will coordinate with Customer to determine a course of action. If the Parties are unable to reach an agreement on a course of action by the day occurring 210 Calendar Days after the filing of the Application, GPC may terminate this DCO Agreement, without obligation or penalty, by providing notice to Customer. Upon such termination, this DCO Agreement will be of no further force or effect, except for any payment obligations of Customer that arose before such termination.
Conditions
. GPC’s obligations under this DCO Agreement, including its obligation to provide the Resiliency Service, are expressly conditioned upon: (i) Customer having completed the Studies to GPC’s reasonable satisfaction; (ii) Customer having executed this DCO Agreement, the Interconnection Agreement, and, if applicable, the EFC Agreement; (iii) Customer’s development, procurement, installation, and ownership of the Customer Equipment as a resource under the DER Customer Owned Schedule; (iv) GPC’s receipt of a fully completed Site Control Affidavit as required under Section 5.1 (Access) for each Site; (v) GPC having determined that the Customer Equipment meets the Minimum Technical Requirements; (vi) the Commission having granted Full and Final Approval; (vii) the completion of, to the reasonable satisfaction of GPC, all associated interconnections, upgrades, modifications, alterations, or replacements to the Electric System required by the Studies or necessary for GPC to perform its obligations under this DCO Agreement (including GPC’s installation of any required GPC Equipment); (viii) the rules and orders of the Commission; (ix) the DER Customer Owned Schedule as approved or subsequently revised by the Commission; (x) the Rules and Regulations; and (xi) the Applicable Standards.
INTERCONNECTION AGREEMENT; EFC AGREEMENT
Interconnection and EFC Agreements
. Customer, contemporaneously with the execution of this DCO Agreement, will execute the Interconnection Agreement and, if applicable, the EFC Agreement for any additional modifications, incremental interconnection, or on-going costs to the Electric System as called for by the Studies, and for which Customer is responsible, to enable GPC to provide the Services. The Interconnection Agreement and, if applicable, EFC Agreement are incorporated by this reference into this DCO Agreement.
EQUIPMENT; RESILIENCY SERVICE AND GRID SUPPORT 
Customer Equipment; Commercial Operation Date
. Consistent with the requirements of this DCO Agreement, the Minimum Technical Requirements, the Applicable Standards, the Interconnection Agreement, the Rules and Regulations, and, if applicable, the EFC Agreement, Customer will engineer, design, procure, install, own, maintain, and make available to GPC the alternative sources of power supply specifically described in the SOW and interconnected allowing GPC to transmit the energy produced to furnish the Services (the “Customer Equipment”). Customer will coordinate with GPC to establish an estimated date upon which the Parties anticipate that the Customer Equipment will be capable of producing electricity to provide the Resiliency Service or Grid Support. GPC will have the right to perform Witness Testing and to exclusively manually or remotely operate the Customer Equipment, including to verify that the Customer Equipment will operate within GPC’s required parameters for GPC’s provision of the Services and in accordance with the Studies. The first Calendar Day of Customer Equipment’s Commercial Operation, as confirmed by GPC in writing, will be the “Commercial Operation Date.” 
GPC Equipment
. Customer hereby grants GPC the right to install any GPC Equipment at the Site, including on or within the Customer Equipment, as GPC deems reasonably necessary for GPC’s provision of the Resiliency Service to Customer and GPC’s provision of Grid Support to the Electric System in support of GPC’s retail customers. 
Resiliency Service
. Commencing upon the Commercial Operation Date and continuing throughout the remainder of the Term, GPC will, as promptly as commercially reasonable, taking into account the operating characteristics of the Customer Equipment and any applicable Operating Procedures, including any applicable responsibilities of Customer at the Site or any then-current operating limitations, dispatch the Customer Equipment to provide Customer with the Resiliency Service during any Outage Event.
Grid Support
. GPC may utilize the Customer Equipment to provide Grid Support and such utilization, subject to Section 4.3 (Resiliency Service) and any applicable provisions of the SOW or the Operating Procedures, may impact or delay GPC’s ability to provide the Resiliency Service in response to an Outage Event. GPC will use commercially reasonable efforts to discontinue the Grid Support and provide Resiliency Service as soon as possible after commencement of an Outage Event, and, in no event will GPC prioritize utilization of the Customer Equipment to provide Grid Support during an Outage Event.  
Operating Procedures
. As soon as reasonably practicable but no less than 90 Calendar Days before the Projected Commercial Operation Date, the Parties will develop, for each Site upon which the applicable Customer Equipment is located, mutually agreeable Operating Procedures for Site activities that GPC reasonably determines may impact: (i) operation of the Customer Equipment; (ii) operation or maintenance of the GPC Equipment; or (iii) performance of the Services. The Operating Procedures will include protocols for: (a) fuel deliveries and fueling of the Customer Equipment; (b) scheduled maintenance and testing of the Customer Equipment and related facilities; (c) notifications and coordination of unscheduled maintenance of such Customer Equipment or facilities; and (d) such other matters as mutually determined by the Parties. The Operating Procedures will also require Customer to promptly notify GPC when Customer has knowledge of any operational issue or damage related to the Customer Equipment or GPC Equipment located at the Site. GPC and Customer will, from time to time throughout the Term, coordinate regarding the further development or refinement of such Operating Procedures.
Fuel Supply and Management
. Throughout the Term, GPC will provide or cause to be provided fuel or necessary commodities (including consumables), as set forth in this DCO Agreement and the SOW, exclusively for use by GPC for the operation of the Customer Equipment. Prior to the Commercial Operation Date, GPC will provide fuel or necessary commodities (including consumables) as reasonably requested by Customer and the cost of such provisions will be paid by Customer within 30 Calendar Days after Customer’s receipt of GPC’s monthly bill reflecting such cost. From and after the Commercial Operation Date and throughout the remainder of the Term, GPC will provide such fuel or commodities at no additional cost to Customer.
PROPERTY RIGHTS
Access
. Customer must coordinate with GPC to grant or obtain, or to obtain on GPC’s behalf and provide to GPC, in coordination with GPC’s land acquisition professionals and GPC’s typical property acquisition process, a right of access to each Site to facilitate GPC’s unfettered access sufficient to allow GPC, in GPC’s sole but reasonable discretion, to: (i) inspect the Customer Equipment (including the right to conduct Witness Testing and to review Customer Equipment design, procurement, construction, installation, commissioning, operation, testing, and maintenance records); (ii) engineer, design, procure, supply, install, interconnect, manage, supervise, inspect, maintain, operate, test, monitor, repair, replace, rebuild, restore, or remove GPC Equipment (including the right to lay down and stage GPC Equipment, tools, materials, other equipment and rigging and to park construction crew vehicles); and (iii) provide any other service or support contemplated or necessary under the Rules and Regulations or this DCO Agreement (collectively, “Access”). Each document granting GPC a right of Access must be: (a) substantially in GPC’s standard form; (b) in conformance with GPC’s standard requirements and acceptable to GPC; and (c) agreed upon in a timely manner. After the Parties have reached an agreement as to the GPC Equipment location(s), GPC will obtain a legal description of the necessary Access locations and provide Customer with an applicable Access form or Site Control Affidavit for execution by the appropriate person. Customer also must obtain and provide mortgage subordinations, as necessary to provide GPC’s rights of Access. Upon receiving any executed documents from Customer, GPC may record such documents or memoranda thereof in the public records of the county where the applicable Site is located, and GPC will be responsible for all applicable costs to record the documents or memoranda. Failure to provide the requested documents in this Section 5.1 (Access) within 90 Calendar Days after the Execution Date will be a material breach of this DCO Agreement, unless such 90-day period is extended in writing by GPC. Customer agrees that it will not take any action (or fail to take any action) that could interfere with GPC’s right of Access.
TITLE; RISK OF LOSS
Title
. Customer Equipment installed at any Site is and will remain, as between the Parties, the sole property of Customer. Any GPC Equipment will remain, as between the Parties, the sole property of GPC.
Modifications
. Customer may not, without GPC’s prior written consent, modify, upgrade, alter, or add to the Customer Equipment during the Term in any manner that could reasonably be anticipated to interfere with GPC’s ability to provide the Services.
Risk of Loss to Equipment
. Customer will bear all risk of loss or damage of any kind with respect to all or any part of the Customer Equipment and GPC Equipment at each Site. 
PERMITS AND MODIFICATIONS
Permits
. Customer will be responsible for obtaining and complying with any license, permit, or approval required to enable the ownership, operation, or maintenance of the Customer Equipment at each Site as necessary to allow each Party to perform under this DCO Agreement and the Interconnection Agreement. GPC agrees to reasonably cooperate with Customer to assist Customer with obtaining and maintaining any such license, permit, or approval. GPC will be responsible for obtaining and complying with any license, permit, or approval required to own, operate, or maintain the GPC Equipment. Each Party will comply with the provisions of any applicable law or regulation. Nothing in this DCO Agreement may be construed as requiring GPC to take any action that would cause it to violate an applicable state or federal regulatory requirement or a condition of a permit. For the avoidance of doubt, the Parties agree that permits issued pursuant to Georgia Administrative Code 391-3-1-.03 are required to be in Customer’s name.
Equipment Maintenance; Alterations
. During the Term, Customer will maintain (or cause to be maintained) the Customer Equipment consistent with such equipment manufacturer’s maintenance standards or such other maintenance standards as may be agreed upon in writing by the Parties and documented in the Operating Procedures. Customer will promptly notify GPC when Customer has knowledge of any operational issue or damage related to the Customer Equipment. Following coordination with GPC, Customer will promptly remedy the operational issue or repair the damage to the Customer Equipment and, thereafter, promptly consult with GPC to allow GPC to confirm the proper restoration of the Customer Equipment. During the Term, Customer will not: (i) operate or test the Customer Equipment (except that Customer may, following prior written notice to and full coordination with GPC, test the Customer Equipment in accordance with the Operating Procedures); or (ii) move, modify, remove, adjust, alter, or change in any material way the Customer Equipment, or any part thereof. Except for GPC Equipment, any replacement of, or alteration or addition to, the Customer Equipment will become part of the Customer Equipment. Customer must also maintain maintenance records, which GPC may review upon reasonable request. Although GPC may review the records and the Customer Equipment, GPC has no responsibility, actual or implied, for Customer Equipment maintenance under this DCO Agreement or otherwise. 
Customer Responsibilities
. Customer must, throughout the Term ensure the Customer Equipment meets: (i) GPC’s Minimum Technical Requirements, including any requirement set forth in the SOW, the Interconnection Agreement, or any applicable EFC Agreement; and (ii) the Commission’s and other applicable legal or regulatory requirements for non-emergency operation. Unless agreed to by GPC in writing, Customer will not modify the Customer Equipment or a Site in a manner that impedes or otherwise interferes with GPC’s ability to provide the Services or in a manner that exceeds the capacity of the Customer Equipment. Customer, at its sole expense, must keep each Site free and clear of anything that could: (a) impair GPC’s ability to: (I) inspect the Customer Equipment; or (II) maintain or inspect the GPC Equipment; (b) impair GPC’s operation or testing of the Customer Equipment or GPC Equipment pursuant to this DCO Agreement; (c) cause damage to the Customer Equipment or GPC Equipment; or (d) impair or otherwise interfere with GPC’s ability to provide the Services.
FINANCIAL TERMS
DCO Credit
. For each applicable Customer account covered by this DCO Agreement and following the applicable Commercial Operation Date, GPC will grant Customer the associated monthly bill credit calculated pursuant to the “Pricing Methodology” provisions of the DER Customer Owned Schedule (the “DCO Credit”) as consideration for GPC’s ability to use the applicable Customer Equipment to provide Grid Support. The DCO Credit will be reflected on the SOW, except that the first and last DCO Credit will be prorated according to the number of days in the applicable calendar month.

The intent of this document is to provide Customer with the GPC’s minimum technical requirements for this system. Customer will use these requirements in developing their technical specifications. Customer is expected to include other requirements as necessary.
The RICE generating system will be manufactured with only new components and materials unless GPC’s prior written approval is obtained.
Each RICE generating system will be either EPA Certified Natural Gas or Tier 4 Final Factory Certified Diesel. 
Operating Requirements
The RICE generating system, including all balance of plant equipment, will be engineered and designed to a minimum design life of twenty (20) years, considering site specific conditions and expected operating conditions.
All facility equipment and systems (mechanical and electrical) will be capable of operation in ambient temperatures between 0°F and 105°F with a coincident humidity between 0% and 100%.
Provisions for winter operation (e.g. freeze protection) will be based on 0°F dry bulb for 72 hours with a continuous 25 mph wind. All facility equipment and systems will be capable of continuous operation under these conditions. 
Customer will identify any limitations on the operation of the RICE generating system including but not limited to limitations such as annual operation hours or annual starts. 
The RICE generating system will automatically startup upon loss of utility at a Customer’s facility. Within 10 seconds from the utility loss, the RICE generating system will provide the required power to meet Customer’s facility load requirement. Upon detection of the return of utility power, the RICE generating system will continue to run for 5-minutes after a return to utility power and then automatically shut down and return to emergency standby and dispatch mode. 
The RICE generating system will also be capable of being dispatched by GPC’s remote dispatch center. Upon receiving GPC’s remote run signal, the RICE generating system will automatically startup and synchronize operation in a parallel interconnection configuration with the grid, with utility export allowed. 

Design Requirements
RICE Design. Customer will be responsible for the design of the RICE system including, but not limited to, determining voltage and kW ratings, quantity of RICE machines required, operational requirements, and any ancillary equipment (paralleling switchgear, fuel tanks, etc.) that may also be required.

For diesel RICE generating systems, Customer will provide adequate storage (minimum of 24-hours), containment, and suitable access and facilities for refill of the fuel supply, in accordance with all applicable codes and regulations.
For natural gas RICE generating systems, Customer will be responsible for interconnection to the existing natural gas supply, including additional piping, valves, fittings and instruments, filtering, and regulation of natural gas supply to the RICE generating system in accordance with all applicable codes and regulations. Customer is responsible for all coordination with the utility.

A grounding system consisting of ground rods and interconnecting copper conductors will be provided for the RICE generating system per industry standards including IEEE 665 and IEEE 80.
All below-grade grounding connections will be exothermic.
The ground grid should be connected to the existing grid in at least 2 places
Synchronizing Controller
A synchronizing controller will be provided by Customer and be capable of tying into a dead bus as well as synchronizing to an energized bus.
Bus PTs will be provided by Customer to support the synchronization scheme.

2.1 The RICE generating system, including all balance of plant equipment, will be engineered and

Customer’s facility load requirement. Upon detection of the return of utility power, the RICE generating
system will continue to run for 5-minutes after a return to utility power and then automatically shut down
and return to emergency standby and dispatch mode.
2.6 The RICE generating system will also be capable of being dispatched by GPC’s remote dispatch
center. Upon receiving GPC’s remote run signal, the RICE generating system will automatically startup and
